messages:
emily: Hey team — just re-auth'd via Okta and now the project console shows me as read-only. I used to be Project Admin. Getting 403 when I try to edit billing settings. 😟

jordan: Sorry you're hitting that. Quick q: did you click the 'Sign in with SSO' button in the console or was this from the browser Okta session restore?

emily: I clicked the Sign in button. I also did a normal Okta MFA flow. Browser is Chrome 117 on macOS.

jordan: Can you paste the exact error or a screenshot? Any console errors? Also which org/project?

emily: Org: acme-analytics, Project: ingestion. Error banner says "403 Permission Denied: insufficient scope". Screenshot pasted. Also seeing a 401→403 transition in network tab when /api/v1/projects/ingestion/members loads.

emily: Network snippet:
```
GET https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/projects/ingestion/members
Response 403
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "description": "token missing required scope: project:write"
}
```

kyle: Hmm. Sounds like the ID token coming back from Okta is missing an application scope or the OIDC claim mapping changed. Did your org recently switch their IdP app from legacy->OIDC?

emily: Not that I'm aware of, but our Okta admin did a generic app update last night. Could be related.

jordan: @sre-oncall can you check the console auth logs for emily's login at 2023-09-09T14:00Z (approx 1694300000)? Looking for token scopes issued and any SCIM group sync events.

sre-oncall: On it. Pulling logs...

sre-oncall: Found auth event: user: emily, idp_session: okta-xxxx, auth_time: 2023-09-09T14:01:02Z, token_type: id_token, scopes: [openid profile email], claims: {email: emily@acme.com, groups: []} — no project scopes present. Also saw a SCIM PATCH for group assignment to project-admins failed earlier: 409 conflict from Okta.

emily: groups: [] ?! But I used to be in project-admins group.

sre-oncall: SCIM logs show Okta tried to update the group mapping at 2023-09-09T13:50Z and received an intermittent 409; Okta retry later, but our system rejected the retry due to an etag mismatch. The group membership change never reached Redwood.

kyle: That explains no groups in the id_token. Without the project-admins group claim our token doesn't include project:write scope, so console treats you as read-only. Two paths: (1) manual fix on Redwood side to re-add emily to project-admins and re-run role sync, or (2) have org Okta admin re-run the SCIM patch/repair. We should also add a retry circuit on our SCIM consumer to handle etag mismatch better.

jordan: For immediate unblock, @sre-oncall can you add emily as Project Admin on ingestion? We should document the root cause and next steps to the customer.

sre-oncall: I can patch the membership. Doing infra auth call: POST /internal/admin/projects/ingestion/members {user: emily, role: project_admin} => 200 OK. User now has project_admin locally.

emily: I reloaded and can edit billing. Thanks!! :tada:

emily: Any way to prevent this from recurring?

sre-oncall: Short-term: ask Okta admin to re-run SCIM sync for the app and check for transient conflicts. We'll raise an internal ticket to improve our SCIM retry logic and to surface failed SCIM patches in the console (we currently only expose full sync errors).

kyle: Also adding a check in auth code: if id_token groups claim is empty but SCIM shows membership for that user, try a forced re-sync once during login to avoid a short window where the IdP and our store diverge. Low risk.

idp-bot: [SCIM] patch_failure detected for acme-analytics app at 2023-09-09T13:50:21Z, status 409, etag_mismatch

jordan: I'll follow up with the customer and include the Okta log snippet + remediation steps. I'll file a support ticket linking this thread and tag infra and auth for the retry fix.
summary: User re-auth via Okta lost project-admin role because SCIM group patch failed (409 etag mismatch). Local fix applied by SRE to re-add user; recommended Okta re-sync and internal SCIM retry improvements.
